title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X/S is a smooth relative curve with ω = Ω^1_{X/S}, and 2 is invertible (the previous page's margin says "2 inv. !"). P = P(P^1_{X/S}(ω)) is the projectivised bundle of principal parts of ω. It is a P^1-bundle with a canonical section σ, coming from the sub-line-bundle ω⊗ω ⊂ P^1(ω). Sections of P disjoint from σ are the splittings of 0→ω^2→P^1(ω)→ω→0. Such a splitting is the same thing as a first-order operator on ω with unit symbol, i.e. a connection on ω. The rank-3 bundle V ≅ Ω⊕Ω^0⊕Ω^{-1} (with Ω ≅ ω) carries the 'admissible' connections, i.e. projective connections, which are sl_2/PGL_2-opers. The proposition on the previous page says: for each section s of P−σ(X) there is exactly one admissible connection for which s is horizontal.

This page asks which projective connections arise this way.
- Work locally. Take a uniformiser t, so dt is a basis of ω. This gives a reference splitting and a reference projective connection c_0, written in a local basis δ of Ω through components ϖ_2, ϖ_1, ϖ_0.
- Write a section as s = s_0 + ω_1. The corresponding splitting v_s is obtained by conjugating with exp θ_{ω_1}; this is a nilpotent sl_2 action, so the expansion stops at the quadratic term.
- Compute the component of c(s) in Ω⊗ω. The result is s_0+ω_1 ↦ c_0 + (δ d(ω_1/δ) + ω_1^2).
- With δ ↦ dt and ω_1 = λ dt this reads s_0+λdt ↦ c_0 + (dλ/dt + λ^2)(dt)^2. He notes 'facteur 2 ?', a normalisation doubt.

Consequence: if a projective connection differs from c_0 by the quadratic differential φ(dt)^2, its horizontal sections of P are the solutions of the Riccati equation λ' + λ^2 = φ. This is the Riccati form of y'' = φy, via λ = y'/y. Equivalently, it is the Miura transformation from connections on ω (or ω^{±1/2}) to sl_2-opers, i.e. the factorisation ∂^2 − φ = (∂+λ)(∂−λ).

Further remarks on the page:
- Over a field of characteristic 0 a solution is determined by its initial data, and a formal solution always exists but is in general transcendental.
- The poles of λ are exactly the points where the horizontal section meets σ. These are the zeros of y, i.e. non-generic relative position.

§1.6 starts the intrinsic version. A section of P is a pair (L, σ: P^1(ω) ↠ L). Such a σ is the same as a first-order differential operator D: ω → L whose symbol γ_0 ∈ Γ(L⊗ω^{-2}) is defined by D(fω) − fD(ω) = γ_0(ω·df). The section meets the canonical section exactly where γ_0 vanishes, i.e. at the singular points of D (continued on the next page).
errors: 'au plus une solution ayant une valeur et une dérivée donnée en un point': for a first-order equation the value alone determines the solution; requiring the derivative too is redundant (or the word is misread).

Normalisation of the quadratic differential is uncertain; Grothendieck himself writes 'facteur 2 ?'. With the bracket conventions of the exp θ expansion, factors of 2 or 1/2 appear, giving λ'+λ^2 versus 2λ' + ... and so on.
The weight attached to ϖ_0 (written ϖ_0 ∈ Γ(Ω^{-1}⊗ω^{4}?)) looks inconsistent with the grading by Ω^{1,0,-1}⊗ω; probably a slip or misreading.
The general formula 'c_0 + (δ d(ω_1/δ·δ^{-1}) + ω_1^2)' is only schematically consistent with the local formula; it is only checked 'sauf erreur'.

ideas.what: Sections of the canonical P^1-bundle P(P^1(ω)) disjoint from the canonical section correspond to splittings of the jet sequence, i.e. connections on ω. Each lies on a unique projective connection making it horizontal.
ideas.modern_name: Miura opers (sl_2), generic relative position of the horizontal Borel reduction and the oper flag
ideas.usually_credited_to: Miura (1968, transformation); Drinfeld–Sokolov (1985); Frenkel (2003–2004, 'Opers on the projective line, flag manifolds and Bethe ansatz')

ideas.what: Horizontal sections of an sl_2-oper relative to a coordinate correspond to solutions of the Riccati equation λ'+λ^2=φ.
ideas.modern_name: Riccati equation / Miura transform φ = λ'+λ^2 (Schwarzian–Riccati relation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Riccati, Schwarz, Klein); in projective-structure language Gunning

ideas.what: Poles of λ correspond to the points where the horizontal section meets the canonical (Hodge) section σ.
ideas.modern_name: Miura opers with regular singularities / non-generic points (Bethe roots)

ideas.what: Sections of P(P^1(ω)) correspond to pairs (L, epi P^1(ω)→L), i.e. first-order differential operators ω→L. The section meets σ at the zeros of the symbol.
ideas.modern_name: Principal parts / jets and differential operators (EGA IV §16)
ideas.where_published: EGA IV §16 (principal parts and differential operators in general; not this specific P^1-bundle application)

ideas.what: Computing the change of projective connection under change of splitting by conjugation with exp of a nilpotent element of sl_2.
ideas.modern_name: Gauge action of the unipotent radical N on opers (Drinfeld–Sokolov gauge)

missed.claim: Around 1972, Grothendieck formulates intrinsically, over a general base S with 2 invertible, the bijection between sections of P minus the canonical section (equivalently connections on ω) and projective connections admitting a horizontal section disjoint from σ. The map is λ ↦ λ'+λ^2, and poles correspond to meeting points with σ. This is the sl_2 Miura-oper picture that Frenkel later made central (Miura opers, Bethe ansatz), predating it by about 30 years and set in the Gauss–Manin/Cartier context.
missed.quote: la question si on peut trouver une section horizontale σ de P ... revient à celle de trouver des solutions λ de l'équation dλ/dt + λ^2 = φ ... Les pôles de une λ correspondent à des pts de rencontre de σ (défini par λ) et de σ'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a relative, characteristic-free (2 invertible) formulation of Miura opers placed next to the Cartier operator. Read with the dossier's Cartier-operator material, it points toward char-p questions such as dormant opers (Mochizuki, Joshi–Pauly, Wakabayashi), where the Riccati/Miura picture and p-curvature interact. This is a historical anticipation rather than a new theorem.

missed.claim: The question of which projective connections (globally) admit a horizontal section disjoint from σ is reduced to the global solvability of a Riccati equation and then left open. He notes that formal solutions are 'transcendantes (!)' and then the text breaks off.
missed.quote: y en a une formelle mais transcendante (!), une singularité qui ne ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Global existence of such sections amounts to reducibility of monodromy or of the oper, a classical topic. The char-p analogue (algebraic solutions, related to p-curvature) is the potentially interesting thread, but it is not developed on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics (Riccati/Miura relation for projective connections) is classical. Grothendieck's intrinsic geometric packaging, however, is exactly the sl_2 Miura-oper framework: sections of the jet P^1-bundle versus the canonical section, uniqueness of the oper making a section horizontal, and poles as non-generic points. That framework was popularised only decades later; a notable but not shocking anticipation.
transcription_corrections: The opening line is likely 'Quelles connexions projectives obtient-on ainsi ?'; the struck phrase is 'Choisissons (local) une uniformisante', with 't de X' kept.
In the exp θ expansion the right-hand side seems to read 'v_{s0} − 2ω_1 v_{s0} + ω_1^2 v_{s0}' (sign uncertain), not '2ω_1 v_{s0} + ω_1^2 v_{s0}'.
'pour v_{s0}' is a margin note ('pour v_{s0} = ...').
'facteur 2 ?' is an interlinear note under the local formula for s_0 + λdt.
'une valeur et une dérivée [?]' is likely 'une valeur donnée en un pt' (the 'dérivée' reading is doubtful).
